definitions.gloss: cooking whole; simmering or boiling an ingredient whole
definitions.explanation: A cooking method where an ingredient is simmered or boiled whole without cutting, filleting, or breaking it apart. Common with small fish, vegetables, and certain fruits.

examples.japanese: {玉|たま}ねぎ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{丸煮|まるに}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
{小|こ}イワシ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{丸煮|まるに}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{骨|ほね}→骨：02166_hone⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{柔|やわ}らかく→柔らかい：01096_yawarakai⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When you simmer small sardines whole, even the bones become soft.

examples.japanese: ⟦トマト→トマト：05192_tomato⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{丸煮|まるに}にして、⟦{崩|くず}し→崩す：03919_kuzusu⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦スープ→スープ：00395_suupu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{美味|おい}しい→美味しい：00740_oishii⟧。
examples.english: Simmering tomatoes whole and breaking them apart into soup is delicious.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{丸|まる}→丸：02167_maru⟧ (whole, entire) and ⟦{煮|に}→煮る：01971_niru⟧ (simmering, boiling). Like ⟦{丸揚|まるあ}げ→丸揚げ：26129_maruage⟧ (whole deep-frying), the ⟦{丸|まる}→丸：02167_maru⟧ prefix emphasizes that the ingredient is cooked without being cut.

Slow simmering (⟦{煮込|にこ}む→煮込む：05822_nikomu⟧) is the key to {丸煮|まるに}, as it allows heat to penetrate throughout the whole ingredient. This method is prized for preserving the shape and natural flavor of the food while making tough parts tender.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸煮|まるに}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to cook whole by simmering
- {玉|たま}ねぎ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{丸煮|まるに}: whole simmered onions
- ⟦{魚|さかな}→魚：00499_sakana⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{丸煮|まるに}: whole simmered fish
- ⟦じっくり→じっくり：06252_jikkuri⟧{丸煮|まるに}: slowly simmered whole

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{丸揚|まるあ}げ→丸揚げ：26129_maruage⟧: whole deep-frying — uses oil rather than liquid to cook the ingredient whole
- ⟦{丸焼|まるや}き→丸焼き：21373_maruyaki⟧: whole roasting — cooking something whole over direct heat
- ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧: simmered dish — the general category of simmered Japanese dishes, usually with cut ingredients
- {姿煮|すがたに}: simmered in its original form — similar concept, typically used for fish presented whole with its shape intact
